newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields Namibia mine closed to March.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields Namibia mine closed to March.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Friday its Kombat mine will only resume production at the end of March due to extensive flooding.
Tsumeb Corporation Ltd (TCL) acting manager Jan du Plessis said by telephone from Namibia that the water pouring into the mine had been stopped since the flooding early last month.

"Production is likely to resume towards the end of March. The water has been successfully stopped, the effect of the water did put us back but we were successful in dewatering the mine so far," du Plessis said.
He said some 2,000 tonnes of copper production would be lost due to the mine closure.
Kombat is one of three mines operated by TCL which were hit by a crippling three-month strike affecting the mines and smelter last year.
TCL said at the time the strike was resolved that it planned to produce around 27,000-28,000 tonnes of blister copper in 1997 and 30,000 tonnes of lead.
Production in 1995 was just under 30,000 tonnes of copper and 27,000 tonnes of lead.
Most of the company's lead is produced from brought-in material while copper output is from the three mines.
Gold Fields Namibia is part of the Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd group.
